2. Satellite Imagery Quality Control Gate

Sentinel-2 L2A BOA surface reflectance timeseries screening evaluated across the property boundary and outer reference ring (tile 21KWP). The STAC query returned 325 items across 189 unique acquisition dates; the 136 extra items are same-day duplicate items of the same tile and orbit (item IDs differ only in the trailing index; processing baselines can differ or repeat), and deduplicate_same_day_scenes selects one item per date by keeping the scene with the highest count of SCL-valid pixels (classes 4, 5, 6, 7) over the read window. STAC metadata investigation revealed that STAC raster:bands offset flags and processing baselines were unreliable for this geographic tile; radiometric BOA offset was consequently detected from raw red band digital numbers (DNs), where scenes with red p1 in [500, 1100) are unresolved and excluded at ingest.

Natural Forest Allowance Cross-Check & Break-Even

At the generous end (T = 0.60) the status stays CONSISTENT for any forest allowance up to 746.62 ha (205.62 ha above the 541.00 ha claim). At the strict end (T = 0.75) the break-even allowance is 256.20 ha, so with 541.00 ha that end already shows a 284.80 ha shortfall; the status rule uses the generous end by design.

Controls: high-canopy pixels stable across all 4 years have 72.5% treecover2000 ≥ 25% and 9.27% loss; the full project boundary has 46.4% treecover2000 ≥ 25% and 8.31% loss; the reference ring has 67.9% treecover2000 ≥ 25% and 4.74% loss. Boundary-wide Hansen tree-cover loss area: 2019: 102.53 ha, 2020: 46.10 ha, 2021: 26.50 ha, 2022: 17.19 ha (total: 192.33 ha). Independent canopy-cover and biomass-proxy change (no canopy claim exists, so unscored)

Between 2019 and 2022, primary canopy cover (qm ≥ 0.70) changed by +94.35% (885.01 ha to 1,720.06 ha; range over threshold grid: +54.94% to +135.81%). Boundary-mean biomass proxy (mean qm NDVI) changed by +24.83% (0.6060 to 0.7565). In the external reference ring, the raw median changed by +8.87% (0.6165 to 0.6712) as background context.

The 2019 baseline composite postdates the 2018 plantings (project start 2018-06), so change since project start is understated.

The biomass proxy is computed on ring-normalised NDVI; the ring change shown is the raw median and is context only, not a quantity to subtract.

NDVI is a proxy that saturates in dense vegetation, and part of the change reflects planting dynamics, not a verified biomass gain.

6. Methodology Limitations

Key methodological and data constraints for this assessment:

  • Satellites verify observable claims (area, planting, canopy), not counterfactual baselines, so avoided-deforestation (REDD+) over-crediting claims are out of reach.
  • NDVI saturates in dense/high-biomass forest and is only a proxy for biomass; upper area thresholds (>= 0.75) sit near saturation for the 2022 project pixels (44.12% have raw NDVI >= 0.85).
  • Strata have no polygons, so spatial verification is plantation mapping inside the estate, not per-stratum checks.
  • The 2018 plantings (and some early-2019 plantings) predate or overlap the Jun-Aug 2019 baseline and cannot be separated from the 541 ha natural forest; the Sentinel-2 L2A record starts about Dec 2018. The 2020 block is the best before/after test but is inconclusive here (144.04-222.63 ha strict vs 310 ha scheduled).
  • The area test depends on a registry-derived forest allowance (541 ha, pdd.pdf p.19) and on NDVI thresholds; the band is 37.72% of the claim, giving a detection limit of 21.91%. Thresholds were chosen, not calibrated.
  • Quantile mapping assumes the ring's distribution is stationary apart from atmosphere/phenology; ring land use changed in 2022 (raw ring p5 0.3937 in 2019 vs 0.2931 in 2022).
  • Only 8-11 dry-season scenes per year.
  • STAC offset/baseline metadata were unreliable for this tile; the offset is detected from DNs (red p1 rule), with a small number of ambiguous scenes excluded.
  • Documented over-crediting cases are contested by Verra, so the flagging-precision sample is small and must be reported honestly.
